findings.text: 需要检查复杂行为断言及保存反例/报告的开发者，目标是对明确模型性质给出可追溯判断。
DSH工具与Skills注册，模型参数/文件读取，schema校验、有限状态探索、报告hash与判定/截断语义。
固定提交的作者材料与关键源码只读核查；未安装或执行目标代码，未运行作者测试，未安排真实宿主验收。引用的既有作者运行记录不视为本轮独立验证。
包清单与固定Git提交核查；npm存在性和下载量以父流程独立META采集为准。

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 首次使用 | Skill上下文、工具定义与构模模型调用 | 学习schema、抽象和性质设计 | 作者有任务成本声明，未独立核对 |
| 持续使用 | 状态枚举资源与模型更新调用 | 维护映射、核对反例和报告diff | 无同条件合格任务成本数据 |
| 失败恢复 | 重构模型/外部检查器资源 | 缩减状态、定位遗漏并重验源码 | 增大maxStates不保证解决，时间未知 |
适合理解有限模型、愿意维护源码映射的工程师小范围试用；未决、跳过关键性质或无法映射实现时停止放行，不把它当自动程序正确性证明。[Q04](#research-q04)

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 可复算报告 | 规范化hash、检查/判定/截断字段 | 模型与源码一致性及全部算法正确性 |
| 全路径性质 | 有限状态探索与反例机制 | 超过边界未决，不能覆盖任意程序 |
| 效果/成本 | 作者报告特定任务成本范围 | 独立任务收益、净节时及质量改进 |
报告语义分层、未知/skip显式和模型hash值得复用。状态引擎与宿主工具分离便于检查，但工具族庞大、构模接口与报告契约维护成本高；本次只核对代表路径，不凭测试目录数量保证引擎正确。
已有增量是把断言核验、有限模型执行、反例和可复算报告接入DSH工作流，报告明确区分跳过、未决和判定；有限状态方法本身及外部检查器不是插件原创。[Q01](#research-q01) [Q02](#research-q02)
忠实抽象是贡献成立的前提。模型pass、规范化hash和工具ok均不能证明源码程序安全；漏掉现实异常或截断搜索时必须收窄结论，构模成本也可能超过简单办法。[Q03](#research-q03)
未验证假设是性质—源码—模型映射—可回放反例的最小证据闭环，能减少模型正确而程序有错的假放行；以已知缺陷和遗漏迁移对照，计入构模/复核成本。[Q04](#research-q04)

technical.rationale: novelty实质增量为多工具报告/Skill集成，非新形式验证算法；mechanism实质增量在拒绝/skip/未决统一语义；transferability实质增量适用于有限协议但需人工抽象；simplification实质增量统一验证与比对，复杂任务收益未测。

business.rationale: workflow实质增量从散文评审转向建模和回放；delivery实质增量为带hash/反例可复算报告；reach实质增量在模型助手中提供形式工具但仍需专业知识；economics小幅增量潜在复核复用，不证明省钱。

recommendation.reason: 理解有限模型边界的工程师可在小协议试用；不用于无源码映射的自动放行。

scenario.rationale: 复杂行为断言与反例交付场景明确

advantage.rationale: 相对纯读代码可获得有限模型可复算判定

evidence.rationale: 代表源码链路可检查但本轮未运行

# DSH Model Everything > 为设计与代码断言提供建模Skill、有限模型验证、UML/依赖审查及可复算报告工具。 ## 研究范围 - **仓库**：[AmethystLuna/dsh-model-everything](https://github.com/AmethystLuna/dsh-model-everything) - **版本号**：0.3.0（[固定提交 1abe8ab4caaf0f0d72553d9ac7054a552c4ff875](https://github.com/AmethystLuna/dsh-model-everything/tree/1abe8ab4caaf0f0d72553d9ac7054a552c4ff875)） - **版本日期**：2026-10-23（固定提交日期，北京时间；不是包发布日期） ## 结论状态 已核查代表性状态验证链路及发布入口；未执行工具，未审计全部算法，模型结论不能外推程序正确。 ## 洞察短评 - **用途**：需要检查复杂行为断言及保存反例/报告的开发者，目标是对明确模型性质给出可追溯判断。 - **亮点**：已有增量是把断言核验、有限模型执行、反例和可复算报告接入DSH工作流，报告明确区分跳过、未决和判定；有限状态方法本身及外部检查器不是插件原创。[Q01](#research-q01) [Q02](#research-q02) - **思考**：忠实抽象是贡献成立的前提。模型pass、规范化hash和工具ok均不能证明源码程序安全；漏掉现实异常或截断搜索时必须收窄结论，构模成本也可能超过简单办法。[Q03](#research-q03) - **建议**：未验证假设是性质—源码—模型映射—可回放反例的最小证据闭环，能减少模型正确而程序有错的假放行；以已知缺陷和遗漏迁移对照，计入构模/复核成本。[Q04](#research-q04) 采用建议：适合理解有限模型、愿意维护源码映射的工程师小范围试用；未决、跳过关键性质或无法映射实现时停止放行，不把它当自动程序正确性证明。[Q04](#research-q04) ## 核心贡献 已有增量是把断言核验、有限模型执行、反例和可复算报告接入DSH工作流，报告明确区分跳过、未决和判定；有限状态方法本身及外部检查器不是插件原创。[Q01](#research-q01) [Q02](#research-q02) ## 关键质疑 忠实抽象是贡献成立的前提。模型pass、规范化hash和工具ok均不能证明源码程序安全；漏掉现实异常或截断搜索时必须收窄结论，构模成本也可能超过简单办法。[Q03](#research-q03) ## 重点创新推演与最小验证 未验证假设是性质—源码—模型映射—可回放反例的最小证据闭环，能减少模型正确而程序有错的假放行；以已知缺陷和遗漏迁移对照，计入构模/复核成本。[Q04](#research-q04) 用带已知异常分支的实现及忠实/遗漏模型，比较假放行、反例回放与人工成本；小模型交叉外部检查器。当前未执行目标代码。 ## 场景与替代办法 需要检查复杂行为断言及保存反例/报告的开发者，目标是对明确模型性质给出可追溯判断。 简单事实用通读或脚本；复杂全路径性质可直接用TLA+/SPIN等检查器。插件贡献是宿主集成与报告契约，未做外部工具效果排名。 ## 依赖与流程 #### 启动与依赖 | 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Node≥20；DSH ^0.1.7-alpha.2 ∨ ^0.1.7-rc.1 ∨ ^0.2.0-rc.1 ∨ ^0.2.1-alpha.1；Cordis ^4.0.4 | 启动必需 | 注册Skills与模型工具 | 以上为作者包声明，本轮未加载；声明范围外兼容未知 | | 忠实模型、明确性质与源码映射 | 效果必需 | 限定判定对象和对应实现 | 缺映射不得把模型pass当程序通过 | | 外部检查器 | 交叉验证/导出后可选 | 复核模型或处理状态爆炸 | 未安装不阻止本地模型检查，外部结论仍未知 | #### 启动步骤 | 步骤 | 执行者与动作 | 成功判据或失败处理 | | --- | --- | --- | | 明确断言 | 用户/助手列性质并核对源码 | 确定不能用简单办法解决且建模有价值 | | 构模与验证 | 助手/工程师选schema并运行指定工具 | 读verdict、truncated、skip和反例，不只看ok | | 回到实现 | 工程师回放反例并冻结报告/模型 | 无映射或未决则停止放行，必要时换检查器 | ## 成本与效果 #### 成本 | 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 首次使用 | Skill上下文、工具定义与构模模型调用 | 学习schema、抽象和性质设计 | 作者有任务成本声明，未独立核对 | | 持续使用 | 状态枚举资源与模型更新调用 | 维护映射、核对反例和报告diff | 无同条件合格任务成本数据 | | 失败恢复 | 重构模型/外部检查器资源 | 缩减状态、定位遗漏并重验源码 | 增大maxStates不保证解决，时间未知 | #### 效果 | 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 | | --- | --- | --- | | 可复算报告 | 规范化hash、检查/判定/截断字段 | 模型与源码一致性及全部算法正确性 | | 全路径性质 | 有限状态探索与反例机制 | 超过边界未决，不能覆盖任意程序 | | 效果/成本 | 作者报告特定任务成本范围 | 独立任务收益、净节时及质量改进 | ## 研究问题与完整回答 **插件研究总目标**：有限模型验证如何把行为断言变成可复算报告，抽象正确性和状态截断如何约束结论？ ### Q01 · 可执行模型审查相对读代码或外部检查器增加什么？ **研究主题**：场景与需求、贡献与相对优势 #### 完整回答 适合需要检查状态机/协议全路径断言、重构前后性质或交付可复算报告的开发者。合格结果不是一段“看起来安全”的解释，而是明确模型、性质、边界、反例与报告hash，并回到源码确认抽象。作者同时提供技能和模型工具，将断言清单、建模、验证、读报告和导出放进DSH，增量在可复算工作流集成与结果语义，不是发明有限状态探索或替代TLA+/SPIN。对人工一次通读或几行脚本即可确定的断言，该方法建模固定成本不合算。README的0.93×–1.11×成本比为作者特定任务报告，本轮没有检查其完整配对实验，不作收益证据。模型检查只能决定输入模型，不自动证明程序实现。结构依赖工具可从源码建图，不应与状态机引擎的抽象责任混淆。 #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 作者声明**：[README.md:11-39](https://github.com/AmethystLuna/dsh-model-everything/blob/1abe8ab4caaf0f0d72553d9ac7054a552c4ff875/README.md#L11-L39) 作者目标、成本声明与模型/程序界线。
查看原文（29行） ```text 把设计与代码里的断言抽象成模型，交给引擎跑一遍：结论带出处与哈希，能复算、能比对。让结论来自一次运行，而不是一次通盘推理：把「想清楚」变成「跑一遍」。 DeepSeek Harness 原生插件。把设计与代码里**关于行为的断言**变成可运行、可审查、可导出的模型： - **核验断言**：逐条对着源码检查，引用到 `file:line`。 - **跑模型**：状态机、协议、多机协作、数据模型先建成可执行模型，再交给引擎跑。 - **审图**：UML 图按模型读、按模型审，并与模型对照。 - **对照重构**：重构前后各建一份模型，两份报告摆一起比。 - **留痕**：结论固化成带哈希的报告，可复算、可比对、可导出。 ## 它更贵，但它给的是判定 这是一个**能力型工具，不是省钱工具**。 **贵多少取决于任务大小，而且是反过来的**：几百行的夹具上它贵出数倍——固定成本（技能正文、工具定义）摊不开；对象涨到几万行、上百文件，比例回落到持平附近，我们测到 0.93×–1.11×。**任务越大，这笔钱越值**：一次判定替代的是几十次 `read`，而不是几行代码。 换来的是别的东西： - 一条**可复算**的结论：哈希、`verdict`、出处，而不是一段读起来像结论的散文； - 一条**反例路径**：哪几步、哪个事件序列让断言不成立； - 一份**可导出的模型**：同一条结论能交给 UPPAAL、TLA+、PRISM、SPIN 复核。 什么时候不值得：断言能靠通读一次代码、或者写三行脚本数出来的时候。**它买不到比读一遍更快**；它买到的是「读一遍给不出判定」的那类断言。 **它判定的是小模型，不是程序。** 引擎显式枚举状态，模型炸开时会报 `truncated` 并点名未决的检查。那不是重试一个更大的 `maxStates` 就能解决的：先减模型（去掉性质不读的变量、合并对称状态），仍然炸开就换不靠枚举的工具——SPIN 的偏序归约、NuSMV 的符号化、CBMC 的有界 SAT。本插件不建立抽象，也不读程序源码。 ## 能力范围 ```
**依据 2 · 作者声明**：[skills/model-everything/SKILL.md:10-25](https://github.com/AmethystLuna/dsh-model-everything/blob/1abe8ab4caaf0f0d72553d9ac7054a552c4ff875/skills/model-everything/SKILL.md#L10-L25) 技能要求断言核验及小模型边界，说明人工建模责任。
查看原文（16行） ```text ## When This Skill Applies **This is the entry point.** Load this skill when a claim about the code has to be settled and a reading will not settle it. It owns the doctrine: enumerate the claims, verify each against the code, cite `file:line`, read `verdict`. It also owns the executable verification for behaviour. A neighbouring domain goes to its own skill through the routing table below. **It decides small models, not programs.** The engine enumerates states, so a model that explodes is reported `truncated` with the undecided check named. That is not a bug to retry with a larger `maxStates`: reduce the model first (drop variables the property does not read, collapse symmetric states), and if it still explodes the property needs a tool that does not enumerate - SPIN for partial-order reduction, NuSMV for symbolic search, CBMC for bounded SAT. This plugin builds no abstraction and reads no program source. **This costs more than reading, and less the larger the task.** On a fixture of a few hundred lines it costs several times a plain reading, because the fixed cost has nothing to amortise against. On a tree of tens of thousands of lines the ratio falls to roughly parity. Spend it where the object is large enough for one decision to replace many reads. Reach for it when the claim is about all paths rather than one, when nothing in the repository will go red if it is false, or when the verdict has to be reproducible later. A claim one reading settles belongs in a sentence, not in a model. | The task involves… | What it does | |---|---| | Any claim about code: design doc, spec, plan, review comment, README, commit message, refactor proposal, "this is safe", "this always holds", "this can't deadlock" | Enumerate the verifiable claims (Phase 1), verify each with `file:line` evidence (Phase 2), classify the gaps (Phase 3) | | A state machine or protocol with three or more states, guards, ACK/NACK/retry, lock/unlock, or start/stop ordering | Build an executable model. Run the S1-S8 structural checks and the A1-A14 adversarial probes | | A quantitative or temporal guarantee: worst-case cost within a budget, "90% of runs reach SAFE", "must leave within 2 ticks" | A12 budget, A13 probabilistic reachability, A14 deadlines. Each returns a counterexample path | | A handshake or power-up sequence across two or more components | `model_compose_verify`: C1 composition deadlock, C2 rendezvous that never fires | | A refactoring that changes state topology or guards | Compare BEFORE and AFTER models for behaviour preservation, invariant continuity and deadlock regression (D1-D4) | | An explicit request to prove code correct, verify a module, or check a migration for breakage | Route by domain through [Routing to the Sibling Skills](#routing-to-the-sibling-skills). Keep the doctrine | ```

本插件**不运行**那个分析，也不对并发安全作任何证明。 一次干净的扫描不是健康证明——它的含义只是没找到声明。 ### 一次迁移：前后两份模型 1. 前后各一份数据模型。 2. 给 `fieldMapping`；来源不是自己旧名字的字段用 `migrationMappings`。 3. `model_datamodel_verify` 查迁移覆盖、拷贝一致性、回滚对称、前后数据回归。 4. `DS2_REQUIRED_FIELD_UNSOURCED` 是 **warning**：它是要你做的决定，不是引擎能替你宣布的失败。 ### 语言包含：两台自动机 1. 把规范与实现各自写成自动机：`states`、`alphabet`、`transitions`、`accepting`。 2. `model_automaton_verify` 带 `other` 与 `relation`（`equivalent` / `subset` / `superset`）。 3. 关系不成立时拿走**最短反例词**——一个实现接受、规范拒绝的词，可以直接在两台机器上重放。 只判有限词。liveness、公平性与时序需要 Büchi 或时间自动机，这个族不做。 ### 图的导入与导出：冻结与迭代 1. `uml_render` 写出 Mermaid / PlantUML 源，`uml_parse` 读回模型。 2. 图源、模型与那次验证的报告一起提交，作为某个时间点的设计记录。 3. 下次改动重抽、重跑，用 `report_diff` 与冻结的那份比对。 4. 要交给外部检查器，用 `model_export` 出 UPPAAL / TLA+ / PRISM / SPIN。 它保留的是**源文件**，渲染出的图片只是副产品。 ## 工具 | 工具 | 做什么 | ## 怎么读报告 工具的产出是一份报告，结论只在 `verdict` 里：**看 `verdict`，不看 `ok`**。`ok` 在各族的含义不同——多数族在评审失败时仍是 `true`，组合族在出现 error 级发现时是 `false`——所以它不能当判定读；把它当判定读，会得出与报告相反的结论。 | 字段 | 说明 | |---|---| | `verdict` | 判定：`pass`、`pass_with_findings`、`fail` | | `verdictReason` | 一句话说明为什么是这个判定 | | `hashes` | `hashSpec` 与 `modelHash`；前后回归另带 `beforeModelHash`、`afterModelHash`。同一份模型永远得到同一个哈希 | | `nextSteps` | 引擎建议的下一步 | | `schema` | 报告的版本化契约，例如 `model-everything/verify/v1`。要按字段分支，就分支在它上面 | | `truncated` | 搜索撞到上限就停了。**截断不等于通过**，是没结论；某个性质没判定出来时，报告里会出现 `_UNDECIDED` | 默认返回正文。被截断的检查可以单独展开：传 `check: ""`，该检查的全部条目都会打印。要完整结果，传 `reportView: "full"`——紧凑 JSON，对象不丢字段。 `ok` 为 `false` 时判定也是 `fail`，但含义不同：工具根本没跑。原因写在 `errorCode` 里——输入不合法、图族不支持，或声明的 `intent` 服务不了。这类拒绝的 `verdictReason` 以 `the tool did not run:` 开头。 报告怎么读，有一份成体系的说明：[`skills/model-everything-report-reading/`](skills/model-everything-report-reading/) 讲阅读顺序（先看跑没跑、再看判了什么、最后看该做什么）、发现分别放在哪一层、以及两处最容易读反的地方。结构由一个**从真实报告生成的思维导图**给出：[`docs/report-reading/mindmap.mmd`](docs/report-reading/mindmap.mmd)，`tests/report-reading` 会在图与引擎不一致时失败。 `uml_render`、`uml_parse`、`uml_review` 另收一个 `intent`，用来说明这份产物要做什么：给人看（`present`）、要被验证引擎读回（`verify`）、还是要证明渲染与模型一致（`fidelity`）。服务不了这个用途的视图会被直接拒绝，而不是勉强画出来。 ## 示例 `examples/` 里是可以直接跑的样本模型，配 `dsh-model-everything` | `dsh-model-everything` | 全部工具与技能 | 开 | | 提示词注入增强 | `dsh-model-everything-gate` | 会话第一条模型步注入一条路由提示 | 开 | **提示词注入增强**是第二个组件，单独开关。它补的是路由的短板：路由靠技能描述文字，而目录行截断在 500 改输入再试；工具没装就明说并退回通用方法——**没有任何东西跑过的检查不是通过的检查**。 它怎么工作，四句话： - **注入点**：`agent/pre-step`，把消息追加到该会话**第一个**模型步的决策里，不是 session-start——后者落进 inbox，可能被空会话的 preset 切换清掉； - **只注入一次**：消息带自己的 producer source - **它只路由**：不检查任何东西，也不会让技能自己加载。 **开关与默认**：默认开。这个默认值是量出来的——它补上的是插件唯一接不住的那类请求，而对照任务没有被过度触发。代价是每个会话约 3.2k 字符；要关掉就改 `cordis.patch.yml`（见下）或翻插件页的开关。想做对照（同一个请求，关一次开一次）也用它。 ## 配置 注入组件（默认开）有三个键： | 键 | 类型 | 默认值 Complex code becomes clear once you model it and run it. Check every claim before you act on it. ## When This Skill Applies **This is the entry point.** Load this skill when a claim about the code has to be settled and a reading will not settle it. It owns the doctrine: enumerate the claims, verify each against the code, cite `file:line`, read `verdict`. It also owns the executable verification for behaviour. A neighbouring domain goes to its own skill through the routing table below. **It decides small models, not programs.** The engine enumerates states, so a model that explodes is reported `truncated` with the undecided check named. That is not a bug to retry with a larger `maxStates`: reduce the model first (drop variables the property does not read, collapse symmetric states), and if it still explodes the property needs a tool that does not enumerate - SPIN for partial-order reduction, NuSMV for symbolic search, CBMC for bounded SAT. This plugin builds no abstraction and reads no program source. **This costs more than reading, and less the larger the task.** On a fixture of a few hundred lines it costs several times a plain reading, because the fixed cost has nothing to amortise against. On a tree of tens of thousands of lines the ratio falls to roughly parity. Spend it where the object is large enough for one decision to replace many reads. Reach for it when the claim is about all paths rather than one, when nothing in the repository will go red if it is false, or when the verdict has to be reproducible later. A claim one reading settles belongs in a sentence, not in a model. | The task involves… | What it does | |---|---| | Any claim about code: design doc, spec, plan, review comment, README, commit message, refactor proposal, "this is safe", "this always holds", "this can't deadlock" | Enumerate the verifiable claims (Phase 1), verify each with `file:line` evidence (Phase 2), classify the gaps (Phase 3) | | A state machine or protocol with three or more states, guards, ACK/NACK/retry, lock/unlock, or start/stop ordering | Build an executable model. Run the S1-S8 structural checks and the A1-A14 adversarial probes | | A quantitative or temporal guarantee: worst-case cost within a budget, "90% of runs reach SAFE", "must leave within 2 ticks" | A12 budget, A13 probabilistic reachability, A14 deadlines. Each returns a counterexample path | | A handshake or power-up sequence across two or more components | `model_compose_verify`: C1 composition deadlock, C2 rendezvous that never fires | | A refactoring that changes state topology or guards | Compare BEFORE and AFTER models for behaviour preservation, invariant continuity and deadlock regression (D1-D4) | | An explicit request to prove code correct, verify a module, or check a migration for breakage | Route by domain through [Routing to the Sibling Skills](#routing-to-the-sibling-skills). Keep the doctrine | | An architecture or dependency question about a component, package or class diagram | `model-everything-structure`: parse it into a dependency graph, judge every edge against the dependency matrix | | Whether a design keeps its own declarations: layering, a responsibility boundary, an interface wider than its callers, a subtype that cannot replace its base | `model-everything-design`: `model_design_review` decides the declared contracts (`DES1`-`DES11`) and reports the graph's shape | **Catalog budget**: DSH renders only the frontmatter `description` and truncates it at 500 characters. Every description here fits. Triggers that do not fit live in this table. ## Verification Depth (Plan-Mode Gate) When loaded as a plan-mode verification gate, this skill's execution is **mandatory**. The model has no discretion to bypass it. Depth classification is gated on objective plan features extracted in Phase 0. ### Phase 0: Feature Extraction (Mandatory) Before any verification, output the plan's feature summary to context: ```text Plan features: Files: [N] Functions added/modified: [list or "none"] Behavioral claims: [none / "invariants listed" / "always/never/guaranteed assertions"] State machine changes: [none / describe topology delta] → Depth: LIGHTWEIGHT | STANDARD | ESCALATED ``` This step is NOT skippable — it creates an explicit, auditable record of what the plan claims before verification begins. ### Depth Classification | Plan Feature | Depth | |-------------|-------| | Single file, zero function signatures added/modified, no behavioral claims of any kind | LIGHTWEIGHT | | Multi-file, OR new/modified function signatures, OR implicit behavioral claims (invariants, equivalence assertions, "behavior is unchanged") | STANDARD | | "Always"/"never"/"guaranteed" language, OR state machine topology changes (≥1 state or ≥2 transitions modified) | ESCALATED | **"No behavioral claims" is narrow**: if the plan asserts anything about behavior preservation — including listing invariants, claiming equivalence, or saying "refactoring only, no behavior change" — that IS a behavioral claim. The absence of the literal words "always"/"never" does NOT mean there are no behavioral claims. ### Output Requirements | Depth | Required | |-------|----------| | LIGHTWEIGHT | All 5 checklist items (file paths, API/type names, line numbers, behavioral claims, mechanism feasibility) answered in context with explicit results per item | | STANDARD | Phase 1-2: enumerate every verifiable claim → verify each against codebase with evidence | | ESCALATED | Full pipeline: Phase 1-5 including Logic Primitive Verification (Phase 2a structural, Phase 2b adversarial) | ### Plan Verification Block After verification, append a summary to the plan file: ```markdown ## Plan Verification - **Depth**: [LIGHTWEIGHT / STANDARD / ESCALATED] - **Scope**: [N] file paths, [M] API/type names, [K] line citations confirmed - **Escalation**: [skipped — no behavioral claims detected] or [see transcript for N-check results] ``` This block is the audit trail. A future reviewer must be able to see what was verified and when. ## Methodology ### Phase 1: Enumerate Claims Read the document fully. Extract every claim that is verifiable: - Numeric claims (counts, sizes, frequencies) - API/type/enum names - File paths and line numbers - Mechanism descriptions ("compile-time resolution", "static dispatch") ### Phase 2: Verify Against Codebase For each claim, run the relevant verification: - **Numeric claims**: `grep -c` or `grep -rn` to get the real count - **API/type names**: extract actual signatures from headers - **Enum/constant values**: list actual values from BSP/config headers - **Mechanism feasibility**: check language standard and compiler support ### Phase 2 Trigger: Escalate to Logic Primitive? If the document under review contains ANY of the following, escalate to [Logic Primitive Verification](#logic-primitive-verification) IMMEDIATELY: - State machine or statechart with ≥3 states OR with guard conditions on transitions - Protocol handshake, ACK/NACK, retry, or timeout sequence logic - Claims using absolute language: "always", "never", "guaranteed", "all paths", "cannot", "impossible" - Lock/unlock, alloc/free, start/stop paired operations where ordering matters - Any logic where correctness depends on transition completeness or event ordering - **Refactoring that modifies state topology**: splitting/merging states, adding/removing transitions, changing guard conditions, extracting sub-machines **Heuristic**: If the transition-to-state ratio > 1.5 or any transition has a guard condition, the machine is complex enough to warrant verification — regardless of state count. For refactoring, trigger if the refactoring changes ≥1 state or ≥2 transitions from the original model. ### Phase 3: Gap Analysis Classify findings by severity: 1. **Architecture-level**: claims that make the design unimplementable (fake APIs, missing modules) 2. **Mechanism-level**: claims the language/compiler cannot fulfill 3. **Consistency-level**: internal contradictions across documents ### Phase 4: Root Cause For each error, identify why it happened: - Wrong mental model (C++ constexpr thinking in C99)? - Incomplete search scope? - Copy-paste from other projects without verification? - Misunderstanding of compiler/linker behavior? ### Phase 5: Structured Output Each finding includes: - Exact location (file:line or section) - What the document claims - What the codebase actually contains (with evidence — grep output, line numbers) - Correction direction --- ## Logic Primitive Verification When Phase 2 triggers escalation, do NOT proceed to Phase 3 until the verification pipeline below is complete. Trust models, not intuition. ### Pipeline Overview ```text Document claims → Extract model → Runtime check: ├── DSH + `model_verify` tool available → build Model schema v1 (references/dsh-model-schema.md) → call the tool → structured report └── No engine available → Manual Verification Mode (see references/logic-verification-guide.md#manual-verification-mode) Refactoring variant: Old code + Refactoring plan → Extract BEFORE model + AFTER model → Run the pipeline on the AFTER model (the same checks) → Compare BEFORE vs AFTER: behavioral preservation, regression, complexity delta → Flag any invariant that held in BEFORE but fails in AFTER UML modelling variant (the task is to draw a flow, not to check a claim): Code flow → model with a citation per element → uml_render → diagram → uml_review → modelling findings + render/parse round-trip fidelity → model_verify → the behavioural checks (S1-S8 / A1-A14) ``` ### Budgeting the Model Before You Run It Search cost is the declared domain times the number of states — and a declared range is not a bound on the search. - **`inc`/`dec` are never clamped to `min`/`max`.** The declaration is a property the checks verify, not a limit the engine enforces. A counter whose guard does not pin it ranges past its own declaration, so the reachable set is unbounded however small the declared range looks; S8 reports that as `S8_DOMAIN_NOT_ENFORCED`. - **Bound a counter with a guard, not a narrower declaration.** `max: 4` with a guard `retry < 4` closes the loop. `max: 4` alone does not. - **Say the budget before running**: values per variable x states. A product in the 10^5-and-up range will hit the cap and come back undecided. - **Model the check where the code performs it.** A cap check that lives inside the tick handler is a guarded branch of the tick event, not a separate event: as a separate event the environment can starve it, and the leads-to failure you then read is an artefact of the model rather than a property of the code. ### Native dsh Tools The tools are `model_verify`, `model_edit`, `model_compose_verify`, `model_datamodel_verify`, `model_design_review`, `model_interleaving_scan`, `model_export`, `report_diff`, `uml_render`, `uml_parse`, `uml_review`, `uml_explain_labels`, `uml_structure_verify` and `model_automaton_verify`. `model_automaton_verify` decides a finite-word language and its relation to another automaton, returning the shortest word that separates them; `references/automata.md` states what each of its checks decides, on what authority, and where it stops. `model_edit` changes a model file by naming the change and returns the structural diff plus the difference in findings, so a fix round costs one call instead of three. `uml_structure_verify` builds its graph from a source tree when given `repoPath`, reading each language's own import construct, so a dependency question about code does not start with drawing. Each tool's description states what it decides and what it does not. Read the description before calling it, and read the report's `verdict` afterwards. A model is the largest argument these tools take. When it is long, or you have edited it more than once, write it to a file and pass `modelPath` instead of inlining it: a streamed argument that long is where invalid JSON comes from, and the file accepts any formatting. These tools carry every capability this plugin claims. Anything outside them is out of scope, and the skills name where that claim is answered instead. ### Reading a Report: `ok` Is Not a Verdict **`ok` records that a report was produced. `verdict` records how the review went.** A report can carry `ok: true` and still be a failed review. Gate on `verdict`. - `pass`: no error and no warning. Report the result as verified, together with the scope the model covered. - `pass_with_findings`: verification ran clean and warnings exist. Report the pass and the warnings. Do not restate it as "no issues". - `fail`: an error finding exists, or the engine rejected the input (`MODEL_INVALID`). State that the claim is not verified, quote the counterexample path, then propose a correction. Do not describe a `fail` as a successful run. `summary.truncated: true` and any code ending in `_UNDECIDED` both mean the search stopped before deciding. Name the invariant that went undecided and report the property as undecided. A tool prints a readable body. Passing checks stay in the `CHECKS` inventory line, and a fact that several checks report appears once. Only error findings inline their evidence. When the body truncates a check, pass `check: ""` to print that check in full. `reportView: "full"` returns the whole report as compact JSON. Use it only to hand the report to `report_diff`; it costs the most tokens of any request you can make. ### Writing the Answer: Name the Finding, Not Its Code `S2_NO_TRANSITIONS`, `UML019`, `DA2` are values of `findings[].code`, not names. A reader who has not memorized the schema learns nothing from one, and cannot tell whether their machine is sound or stuck. - **Say what it means**, in the user's language and in the terms of their own code: 「启动超时后 ERROR 没有任何出口迁移，机器会停在那里」, not 「S2 命中」. The finding's `message` is written for the report; the sentence for the user is written from it. - **Keep the identifier where the identifier is the subject**: a report field quoted verbatim, a baseline diff, a test name, or a question about the check itself. - **Name the property, not the checking.** "This path locks without unlocking" beats "A4 failed". A check's name earns its place when the reader asked about the checking. - **Carry the verdict in words.** "Not verified" or "verified, within the scope of this model" — never a bare pass, and never a warning presented without its label. A reader who cannot tell what failed will either trust a report they cannot read, or ignore one they should act on. ### Slice Acceptance: Baseline Diffs The acceptance criterion for a refactoring slice is usually "no **new** findings", not "zero findings". Do not compare two JSON reports by eye — run the comparison: - DSH: `report_diff { baseline: , current: }` - Any host without the tools: run the repository engine against the same JSON. (also available on `compose`, `structure` and `uml-review`) A finding's identity is its **check id + code + canonical locator** (built from `evidence`/`path`; the message only when a finding carries neither), so a reworded message reads as `changed`, never as a new finding. The diff's `verdict` describes the **delta** — a newly added error finding fails it — while `currentVerdict` keeps the absolute result visible, and a clean delta over a still-failing report says so in `nextSteps` rather than passing quietly. Two runs over the same input add zero findings: run that self-check before trusting any baseline. ### Archiving a Model: `_`-Prefixed Metadata Keep provenance with the model instead of in a sidecar that drifts: - Any key starting with `_` at any level (`_source`, `_verified`, `_uml`, `_extraction_caveats`, `states[0]._note`) is **annotation metadata**: the schema ignores it, `modelHash` excludes it, and the report echoes it as `metadataKeys`. - Everything else stays closed — a mistyped `sttes` is still a validation error, and that is deliberate. - Because the hash ignores `_` keys, "the model as archived" and "the model with metadata stripped" hash identically; record the reported `hashSpec` next to the hash so a later reader can reproduce it (`verify model.json --hash-check ` answers whether a recorded hash belongs to a published spec at all). ### Refactoring Verification Mode When the document under review is a refactoring plan (modifying existing state machine logic, not designing from scratch), adapt the pipeline: 1. **Extract the BEFORE model** from the existing codebase (not the plan — verify what the code actually does, not what the plan claims it does) 2. **Extract the AFTER model** from the refactoring plan 3. **Show both tables AND their model narratives** to the user side by side and confirm the delta is intentional 4. **Run Phase 2a + 2b on the AFTER model** — the same checks a new design gets 5. **Compare BEFORE vs AFTER**: | Check | Method | Severity if Violated | |-------|--------|:---:| | Behavioral preservation | Every event sequence accepted by BEFORE must also be accepted by AFTER (or explicitly removed per plan) | Error — regression | | Invariant continuity | Any invariant that held in BEFORE must hold in AFTER (unless the refactoring explicitly changes it) | Error — undocumented behavior change | | Deadlock regression | New states or transitions must not introduce deadlocks not present in BEFORE | Error | | Complexity claim | If plan claims "simpler": count states + transitions + guards. Is AFTER objectively simpler? | Warning — unsubstantiated claim | | Unreachable code | New states added in AFTER must be reachable (otherwise they're dead code from the start) | Warning | In DSH, pass `beforeModel` and optional `stateMapping` to `model_verify`; the engine runs D1 Behavioral Preservation, D2 Invariant Continuity, D3 Regression Delta, and D4 Deadlock/Liveness Regression automatically. 6. **Flag any behavioral delta not documented in the plan** — the most common refactoring bug is an unintended side effect that the plan doesn't acknowledge Run the checks with the native `model_verify` tool (model JSON, structured guard DSL, path-aware invariants) — see `references/dsh-model-schema.md`. A host without the tools can run the repository engine against the same JSON. For probe patterns, extraction methodology and manual procedures, load `references/logic-verification-guide.md`. ### Phase 2a: Structural Primitives Run these FIRST. They establish basic well-formedness before adversarial probing. | # | Primitive | Method | Severity if Violated | |:--:|-----------|--------|:---:| | S1 | **Reachability** | BFS from init state; flag all states not in visited set | Warning — dead code | | S2 | **Deadlock** | Any non-terminal state with zero outgoing transitions? | Error — machine can get stuck | | S3 | **Liveness** | Does the transition graph contain an absorbing cycle that excludes expected terminal/recovery states? (e.g. ERROR→RECOVERING→ERROR→... with no exit) | Error — infinite loop | | S4 | **Determinism** | Same state + same event → multiple different targets? | Error — ambiguous behavior | | S5 | **Event completeness** | For each state, are there plausible events with no defined transition? | Warning — implicit ignore | | S6 | **Guard completeness** | For each transition with a guard condition, are ALL branch outcomes defined? `if (cnt<3) RETRY else FATAL` → both paths must exist in model | Error — undefined behavior path | | S7 | **Invariant validity** | Does every reachable state satisfy the plan's stated "always/never/guaranteed" assertions? | Error — plan claim is false | | S8 | **Monotonic variables** | If a variable is declared `monotonic: inc/dec`, do all updates respect that direction? | Error — counter can move backwards | ### Phase 2b: Adversarial Probes Run these second. Each probe tries to break the model, and a probe that finds a violation proves a behaviour gap. | # | Attack | Method | Claim it refutes | |:--:|--------|--------|-------------| | A1 | **Unexpected event** | Inject every event E into every state S that has no transition for (S, E). Record whether the model ignores it or crashes. | "All events are handled in all states" | | A2 | **Race interleaving** | Deliver every pair of concurrent events in both orders. Report a differing terminal state. | "Behaviour is independent of ordering" | | A3 | **Order permutation** | Permute N independent events. Report differing final states or broken invariants. | "Outcome is order-independent" | | A4 | **Pair symmetry** | Match every `start/stop`, `lock/unlock`, `alloc/free` pair. Report a path where a pair is unbalanced. `onEntry` and `onExit` count as acquire and release. | "Resources are always released" | | A5 | **Boundary blast** | Probe counters at 0, 1, max-1, max and max+1, and timestamps at 0 and wraparound. Report overflow, underflow or undefined behaviour. | "Handles all counter and timer values" | | A6 | **Resource injection** | Simulate `malloc` returning NULL, a full queue and a semaphore timeout at each state that calls them. Report a state with no recovery path. | "Degrades gracefully under resource pressure" | | A7 | **Counter-example witness** | For a failing invariant, emit the exact violating sequence. The breadth-first searches (state, sequence, atomicity, budget) return the shortest witness. Leads-to and probability return the witness they found without claiming minimality. | "This invariant holds" | | A8 | **Idempotent replay** | Apply each `idempotentEvents` entry twice from every reachable state. Report a second application that changes state. | "This event is safe to replay" | | A9 | **Leads-to** | From a declared source state, every path must reach the target state or a member of the declared target set. | "Always progresses to completion" | | A10 | **Sequence order** | Declared events must occur in the declared order. | "backup before modify before commit" | | A11 | **Atomicity** | An atomic event must commit or roll back before the scope is left or the machine terminates. | "all-or-nothing" | | A12 | **Budget** | With `cost` per transition (absent means 1) and a `budget` invariant, every reachable path must stay within budget.
